headline: Stoke win, create little — and the market stays careful
summary: Stoke City have won four of their last five Championship games and sit sixth on 19 points, but the wins hide a thin attacking game: 0.83 expected goals per match. Bristol City arrive after two 0-1 home defeats, so the recent runs point in opposite directions. Yet Bristol City are creating 1.44 expected goals a game, more than Stoke, which is why the market, across 10 bookmakers with the margin removed, makes Stoke only 41.1% favourites and rates them a quarter of a goal better, 0.25. Over 2.5 goals is close to even at 49.3%.
read: Stoke City are sixth and have won four of their last five, and they host a Bristol City side that has lost its last two home games 0-1 and sits 16th. The market calls it close — Stoke a narrow 41.1% favourite and rated only a quarter of a goal better, with goals a genuine coin flip.

facts.fact: Stoke City are priced as 41.1% favourites to win at home.
facts.meaning: They are the more likely winners but well short of a clear favourite — this is a tight game, not a mismatch.

facts.fact: Stoke have won four of their last five Championship matches, most recently 1-0 away at Derby County.
facts.meaning: They come into a home double-header with real momentum and sit sixth in the table.

facts.fact: Stoke are averaging only 0.83 xG per game across their last five matches.
facts.meaning: The wins have come without much chance creation — they were heavily out-created at Bolton and still won 2-1.

facts.fact: Bristol City are averaging 1.44 xG per game across their last five matches — comfortably more than Stoke have been creating.
facts.meaning: They are generating enough to trouble Stoke; the problem has been putting the chances away, with two goals in that run.

facts.fact: Bristol City have lost their last two home games 0-1, to Blackburn Rovers and Sheffield United.
Stoke sit sixth in the Championship on 19 points from 11 games.
facts.meaning: A win keeps them in the play-off places; Bristol City are five points behind in 16th.

facts.fact: Stoke's last five matches have produced 15 goals, three per game.
facts.meaning: Their games have been open at both ends; Bristol City's last five have produced far fewer goals.

facts.fact: Over 2.5 goals is priced at 49.3% — the market is split on whether this game reaches three goals.
facts.meaning: There is no clear goals lean either way; both teams to score is also favoured at 54.6%.

sources.fact: Stoke City have won six of their last eight Championship matches and sit sixth in the table.
Stoke beat Derby County 1-0 away in their most recent match, with Luke Graham scoring his first goal for the club.
Stoke defender Luke Graham says the in-form Potters are "not looking back" after turning their form around.
BBC Radio Stoke's Mark Elliott says Luke Graham and Stoke City continue to improve after their win at Derby.
Mark Robins is Stoke City's manager.
Bristol City have suffered back-to-back home defeats at Ashton Gate, to Blackburn Rovers and Sheffield United.
Bristol City fan and podcaster Richard Angell says his patience with the club has evaporated and that constant change at Ashton Gate should be bringing better results.
Bristol City boss Michael Skubala says he wants to dent Stoke City's home form and described Stoke as "very physical", namechecking three players.
